title: Derive SCREEN_TO_FLOW from SCREEN_TRIGGERS instead of a second hand table
body:
## Summary
The screen-node to flow-node mapping is kept twice: SCREEN_TO_FLOW in data.ts and the screen/flowNode pairs of SCREEN_TRIGGERS in hudRegistry.ts.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/_shared/data.ts:109 hand-lists 7 screen->flow pairs; 5 of them (inventory, char-stats, pause, enemy-bars, damage-numbers) are also declared in src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/_shared/hudRegistry.ts:142 SCREEN_TRIGGERS. Row selection (screenWorklist.ts flowIdForScreenNode / screenNodeForFlow), the row highlight (FlowNodesTab.tsx getScreenHighlightColor) and the catalog entity a row drives all read SCREEN_TO_FLOW, while flow edges read SCREEN_TRIGGERS. Renaming a flow node in one table silently unbinds rows from their catalog screen. Fixed: SCREEN_TO_FLOW = the 2 HUD child rows + SCREEN_TRIGGERS projected, with a test that every trigger screen resolves to its own flow node.

## Flow
- rename flowNode "CharStats" in SCREEN_TRIGGERS
- the flow graph edge follows; SCREEN_TO_FLOW still says CharStats
- the char-stats row now highlights a node with no edge and the graph node has no row
- fix: project SCREEN_TO_FLOW from SCREEN_TRIGGERS + HUD_CHILDREN, pin with a parity test

## Expected impact
Designers editing the registry stop desynchronising rows, graph and catalog binding; measured as duplicated pairs 5 -> 0. Could break: seed-screen-flow ids if a flowNode spelling changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one owner for the screen->flow join
Before: 5 of 7 screen->flow pairs declared in two tables (data.ts:109, hudRegistry.ts:142)
After: 0 duplicated pairs predicted; screenWorklist.test.ts cases 1-2 must stay green
Method: simulation - walked the rename case; not built this round because data.ts is imported by seed-screen-flow.ts outside the paths and the change needs its seed tests run
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Designers editing the registry stop desynchronising rows, graph and catalog binding; measured as duplicated pairs 5 -> 0. Could break: seed-screen-flow ids if a flowNode spelling changes.
instrument: parity test: for every SCREEN_TRIGGERS t, flowIdForScreenNode(t.screen) === t.flowNode; seeded by renaming one flowNode

title: Flow graph draws each Input Action label twice on one spot
body:
## Summary
Every Input Action screen gets an open edge and a dashed close edge with the same label over the same line, so 3 labels are painted twice at one midpoint.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/_shared/data.ts:150-151 builds FLOW_EDGES as HUD->screen plus screen->HUD for every trigger with an action, both labelled triggerLabel(t). src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/flow/FlowGraph.tsx draws the label at the shared midpoint (mx, my-6) for both, so Inventory, CharStats and Pause each stack two identical texts and two lines exactly on top of each other; the dashed return edge is invisible under the solid one. Fixed: offset the pair perpendicular to the edge (as UIBindingsTab already does for its SM edges, perpX/perpY) and label only the open edge.

## Flow
- open Screen Flow tab
- look at HUD->Inventory edge
- two text nodes "IA_OpenInventory (Tab / I)" at identical x/y, dashed return line hidden

## Expected impact
The return transition becomes visible in the graph; measured as overlapping label pairs 3 -> 0. Could break: label legibility on the short HUD-adjacent edges.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - both directions of a screen transition are visible
Before: 3 of 8 edge labels coincide with another label (same text, same x/y)
After: 0 coincident labels predicted with a perpendicular offset
Method: simulation - derived from FLOW_EDGES construction and FlowGraph label placement; geometry test like flowGraph.geometry.test.tsx would decide it
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/_shared/data.ts:150-151
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/flow/FlowGraph.tsx label at (mx, my - 6) for every edge
impact: The return transition becomes visible in the graph; measured as overlapping label pairs 3 -> 0. Could break: label legibility on the short HUD-adjacent edges.
instrument: render test counting <text> nodes sharing x,y in the flow SVG (3 today)

title: Localization overflow list names widgets the HUD registry does not know
body:
## Summary
LANGUAGES.overflowWidgets names AbilityTooltip and QuestDescription, neither of which resolves through the HUD registry, and validateHudRegistry never checks this list.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/_shared/data.ts:220-226 hand-lists overflow widgets per language; resolveWidgetId("AbilityTooltip") and resolveWidgetId("QuestDescription") are undefined (registry has Tooltip and QuestTracker, hudRegistry.ts:67-113). The registry lint (hudRegistry.ts:282) covers contexts only, so this third widget-naming table escapes the one-owner rule the registry doc comment claims. Fixed: name registry ids (or add aliases) and extend validateHudRegistry with an unknown-widget issue for language overflow names.

## Flow
- open Accessibility tab, pick DE
- overflow chips show AbilityTooltip, QuestDescription
- neither exists in the HUD widget registry, Z-layers or bindings

## Expected impact
The overflow preview points at real widgets; unresolved names 2 -> 0 and the lint catches the next one. Could break: chip text changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every widget name in the module resolves to a registry widget
Before: 2 of 2 distinct overflow names unresolved (resolveWidgetId returns undefined)
After: 0 unresolved, pinned by a lint case
Method: probe - read both names against HUD_WIDGETS ids and aliases; not built because which registry widget a "QuestDescription" is needs a design call
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The overflow preview points at real widgets; unresolved names 2 -> 0 and the lint catches the next one. Could break: chip text changes.
instrument: hudRegistry.test.ts case: every LANGUAGES overflow name resolves via resolveWidgetId

title: Feature Map toggles for arpg-ui gate the wrong tabs and 3 of 7 do nothing
body:
## Summary
The arpg-ui Feature Map sections do not match the tabs they hide: Systems is gated by "breakpoints", UI by "animations", and edges/bindings/z-layers have no consumer.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/index.tsx:90,95,100 gate the Systems tab by sectionId "breakpoints", the UI Bindings tab by "animations" and Accessibility by "categories". Breakpoints and bindings actually render in UIBindingsTab, z-layers in SystemsTab. src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/feature-map-config.ts:137-145 declares 7 sections; grep for sectionId="edges"|"bindings"|"z-layers" inside sub_ui returns 0 consumers (the only "bindings" consumer is sub_character InputTab). The HUD Preview tab is ungated. Fixed: section ids named after what each tab holds, sub-sections wired or removed.

## Flow
- Feature Map: turn off "Breakpoints"
- the whole Systems tab (budgets, z-order, compositor) disappears; the breakpoint table in UI Bindings stays
- turn off "Z-Layers": nothing changes

## Expected impact
Visibility toggles do what their labels say; dead toggles 3 -> 0. Could break: persisted visibility prefs keyed by old ids.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every visibility toggle hides the content it names
Before: 3 of 7 arpg-ui sections have 0 consumers; 2 of 4 gated tabs hidden by a section named for other content
After: 0 dead sections, each gate named for its tab
Method: probe - grep of VisibleSection sectionId across src/components; out-of-scope: feature-map-config.ts belongs to core-engine-genre-tabs
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/index.tsx:90 sectionId="breakpoints" wraps <SystemsTab />
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/index.tsx:95 sectionId="animations" wraps <UIBindingsTab />
src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/feature-map-config.ts:137-145
grep sectionId="(edges|bindings|z-layers)" -> only sub_character/input/InputTab.tsx:44
impact: Visibility toggles do what their labels say; dead toggles 3 -> 0. Could break: persisted visibility prefs keyed by old ids.
instrument: test: every feature-map-config arpg-ui section id has >=1 VisibleSection consumer under sub_ui

title: WBP starter class chips hide which class is selected from assistive tech
body:
## Summary
The six HUD class chips in WBPStarterPanel show selection by background opacity only (no aria-pressed), and the class input removes its outline with no focus replacement.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/wbp-starter/WBPStarterPanel.tsx chip buttons set backgroundColor by targetClass === c with no aria-pressed; the input carries className outline-none and no focus-ring. Same defect class fixed this round in ArpgHudPreview and the compositor toggle (commits b61c9fc5, 96b1e1d5). Fixed: aria-pressed on chips, focus-ring on input and chips.

## Flow
- tab to the class chips with a screen reader
- each chip announces "button" with no pressed state
- focus on the input is invisible

## Expected impact
Keyboard and screen-reader users can tell the chosen class; 0/6 -> 6/6 chips expose state.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - selection state is exposed, not colour-only
Before: 0 of 6 chips carry aria-pressed; input focus outline suppressed
After: 6 of 6 predicted with a one-attribute change
Method: probe - read the 6 rendered chips; not built for round budget
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/wbp-starter/WBPStarterPanel.tsx chips: style backgroundColor targetClass === c, no aria-pressed; input className "... outline-none"
impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users can tell the chosen class; 0/6 -> 6/6 chips expose state.
instrument: wbp-starter-panel.test.tsx case: clicked chip has aria-pressed=true, others false

title: ARPG HUD preview is mounted twice: its own tab and inside Systems
body:
## Summary
ArpgHudPreview renders both as the HUD Preview tab and again at the bottom of the Systems & Constraints tab.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/index.tsx:104 mounts <ArpgHudPreview /> for the hud-preview tab, and src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/systems/SystemsTab.tsx:274 mounts it again between the Z-order panel and the compositor. Two copies, two independent selections. Which tab owns the preview is a product call (direction): drop it from Systems, or drop the tab.

## Flow
- open Systems & Constraints
- scroll: ARPG HUD Layout panel
- open HUD Preview: the same panel

## Expected impact
One home for the preview; mounted copies 2 -> 1. Could break: anyone relying on seeing it beside the compositor.

## Evaluation
Claim: other - one home per surface
Before: 2 mounts of ArpgHudPreview in one module
After: 1 mount
Method: probe - grep of <ArpgHudPreview in sub_ui (2 hits)
Result: better
Gate: direction
impact: One home for the preview; mounted copies 2 -> 1. Could break: anyone relying on seeing it beside the compositor.

title: Widget performance budget shows fixed numbers as if measured
body:
## Summary
Three of four Widget Performance Budget bars (VertexCount 800, DrawCalls 12, TextureMemory 24MB) are constants, rendered with percent and warn/danger colours like a measurement.

## Description
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/_shared/hudRegistry.ts:251-255 STATIC_BUDGETS hard-codes current values; only Bindings (hudRegistry.ts:258) is derived from the registry. src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/systems/SystemsTab.tsx:218-236 paints them with thresholds, so a green bar asserts a budget nobody checked. Same class as the recorded accessibility-score deviation (data.ts A11Y_OVERALL_SCORE), on a different surface. Fixed means a measured source (UE widget stats / a profiling artefact) or an explicit "estimate" marking: choosing which is a direction call.

## Flow
- open Systems & Constraints
- VertexCount 800/2000 40% green
- no code path measures it

## Expected impact
The budget panel stops claiming health it has not observed; measured-or-labelled bars 1/4 -> 4/4.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - a budget bar is a measurement or says it is not
Before: 3 of 4 budget bars are constants shown as measurements
After: 0 unlabelled constants
Method: probe - read every BudgetBar source; unmeasurable which data source should feed it without an owner decision
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/_shared/hudRegistry.ts:251 { label: 'VertexCount', current: 800, ... }
src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ui/_shared/hudRegistry.ts:258 performanceBudgets() derives only Bindings
impact: The budget panel stops claiming health it has not observed; measured-or-labelled bars 1/4 -> 4/4.
